Confidence Interval for the Difference Between Two Paired Proportions

Source: R/ci_proportion_paired.R
ci_proportion_paired.Rd

Computes a confidence interval for the difference between two proportions measured on the same units, \(\psi = p_x - p_y\): two diagnostic procedures applied to the same patients, the proportion of students answering an item correctly before and after instruction, or two raters' rates of assigning a category to the same cases. The two outcomes of a unit are correlated, so the interval for two independent proportions does not apply. The default is the score interval of Tango (1998), which inverts the score test of Nam (1997). It stays inside \([-1, 1]\) and is defined when no pair is discordant. When discordant pairs are rare, as in the case worked through under Details, it covers the difference more often than its nominal level, erring on the conservative side, where the familiar Wald interval falls well short of that level.

Usage

ci_proportion_paired(
  x = NULL,
  y = NULL,
  n_10 = NULL,
  n_01 = NULL,
  N = NULL,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  method = c("score", "wald")
)

Arguments

x, y

Numeric or logical vectors of the same length, one element per unit, coded 1 (success) and 0 (failure): the outcome of each unit under the first condition (x) and the second (y). A pair with a missing value in either vector is dropped. Supply either x and y or the three counts, not both.

n_10

Number of units that succeed under x and fail under y.

n_01

Number of units that fail under x and succeed under y.

N

Number of units (pairs), at least n_10 + n_01.

conf_level

Confidence level. Defaults to 0.95. A conf_level of 0.90 gives the interval whose limits are the one-sided 95% bounds read in noninferiority and equivalence decisions.

method

"score" (default; Tango, 1998) or "wald".

Value

A data.frame (class dmar_tbl) with rows ci_lower, difference (\(\hat\psi\)), ci_upper, n_10, n_01, and N, so the point estimate sits between its confidence limits. The confidence level is the conf_level attribute and the interval's method the method attribute.

Details

Only the discordant pairs carry the difference. Classify the \(N\) units by their pair of outcomes: \(n_{11}\) succeed under both conditions, \(n_{10}\) under x only, \(n_{01}\) under y only, and \(n_{00}\) under neither. The two proportions are \((n_{11} + n_{10})/N\) and \((n_{11} + n_{01})/N\), so \(n_{11}\) cancels from their difference, \(\hat\psi = (n_{10} - n_{01})/N\), and the concordant units enter only through \(N\). That is why the counts interface asks for n_10, n_01, and N and nothing more. The variance of the per-unit difference, \(p_{10} + p_{01} - \psi^2\), depends on a discordant probability as well as on \(\psi\), so for inference on \(\psi\) the probability \(p_{01}\) is a nuisance parameter.

The score interval. For a hypothesized difference \(\psi_0\) the score statistic is $$Z(\psi_0) = \frac{n_{10} - n_{01} - N\psi_0} {\sqrt{N\{2\tilde p_{01} + \psi_0(1 - \psi_0)\}}},$$ where \(\tilde p_{01}\) is the maximum likelihood estimate of \(p_{01}\) under the restriction \(p_{10} - p_{01} = \psi_0\), the larger root of a quadratic (Nam, 1997, equations 1 and 3). The denominator is \(N\) times the variance of the per-unit difference, evaluated at the restricted estimates rather than at the observed proportions. With \(\alpha\) = 1 - conf_level, the lower limit is the value of \(\psi_0\) at which \(Z(\psi_0) = z_{1-\alpha/2}\) and the upper limit the value at which \(Z(\psi_0) = -z_{1-\alpha/2}\), found by root finding. At \(\psi_0 = 0\) the statistic is McNemar's, \((n_{10} - n_{01})/\sqrt{n_{10} + n_{01}}\), so the score interval excludes 0 exactly when McNemar's test without a continuity correction rejects at level \(\alpha\): the interval extends that test to every other value of the difference. With no discordant pair the limits are \(\mp z^2/(N + z^2)\), with \(z = z_{1-\alpha/2}\), an interval whose width reflects the \(N\) units observed rather than a width of zero.

The Wald interval. The interval \(\hat\psi \pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\{(n_{10} + n_{01})/N - \hat\psi^2\}^{1/2}/\sqrt{N}\) estimates the variance at the observed proportions instead, and is available for instruction and comparison. With few discordant pairs it is too short: it has zero width when no pair is discordant, and it can extend beyond \([-1, 1]\). Nam (1997) found by simulation that the test it inverts rejects more often than its nominal level, while the score test holds close to the nominal level and tends to the conservative side. Summing over every possible table with \(p_{10} = .03\), \(p_{01} = .01\), and \(N = 50\), the 95% score interval covers \(\psi\) with probability .986 and the 95% Wald interval with probability .779.

Noninferiority and equivalence. The limits of a 100(1 - 2\(\alpha\))% interval are one-sided 100(1 - \(\alpha\))% confidence bounds, so conf_level = 0.90 gives the interval that equivalence_proportion_paired reads against its bounds at alpha_level = 0.05.

References

McNeil, B. J., Keeler, E., & Adelstein, S. J. (1975). Primer on certain elements of medical decision making. New England Journal of Medicine, 293(5), 211–215. doi:10.1056/NEJM197507312930501

Nam, J.-m. (1997). Establishing equivalence of two treatments and sample size requirements in matched-pairs design. Biometrics, 53(4), 1422–1430. doi:10.2307/2533508

Tango, T. (1998). Equivalence test and confidence interval for the difference in proportions for the paired-sample design. Statistics in Medicine, 17(8), 891–908. doi:10.1002/(SICI)1097-0258(19980430)17:8<891::AID-SIM780>3.0.CO;2-B

See also

equivalence_proportion_paired for noninferiority and equivalence tests on the same difference; ci_proportion for a single proportion; responder_analysis for two independent proportions; mcnemar.test for the test of no difference.

Other confidence intervals: ci_crossed(), ci_proportion(), ci_two_phase()

Author

Ken Kelley kkelley@nd.edu

Examples

# Liver scan data from McNeil, Keeler, and Adelstein (1975), the
# example of Nam (1997, p. 1427): 344 patients classified as positive
# or negative by scan (x) and by pathology (y). Only the 32 and 27
# patients on whom the two disagree inform the difference in the
# positive rates.
liver <- matrix(c(231, 27, 32, 54), nrow = 2,
                dimnames = list(scan = c("positive", "negative"),
                                pathology = c("positive", "negative")))
liver
#>           pathology
#> scan       positive negative
#>   positive      231       32
#>   negative       27       54
ci_proportion_paired(n_10 = liver["positive", "negative"],
                     n_01 = liver["negative", "positive"],
                     N = sum(liver))
#>  term       value 
#>  ci_lower   -0.030
#>  difference 0.015 
#>  ci_upper   0.059 
#>  n_10       32    
#>  n_01       27    
#>  N          344   
#> 
#> Confidence level: 95%

# From raw outcomes: two judges assign the same 200 cases to one of
# three diagnoses. diagnosis_agreement holds one row per cell of their
# agreement table, so repeating each row by its frequency gives one row
# per case. How much more often does Judge A (x) than Judge B (y)
# diagnose a personality disorder?
cases <- diagnosis_agreement[rep(seq_len(nrow(diagnosis_agreement)),
                                 diagnosis_agreement$frequency), ]
ci_proportion_paired(x = cases$judge_a == "Personality disorder",
                     y = cases$judge_b == "Personality disorder")
#>  term       value
#>  ci_lower   0.036
#>  difference 0.100
#>  ci_upper   0.166
#>  n_10       32   
#>  n_01       12   
#>  N          200  
#> 
#> Confidence level: 95%

# When the two conditions agree on all 40 units, the Wald interval has
# zero width, as though the difference were known exactly; the score
# interval still reflects how few units were observed.
ci_proportion_paired(n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, N = 40)
#>  term       value 
#>  ci_lower   -0.088
#>  difference 0.000 
#>  ci_upper   0.088 
#>  n_10       0     
#>  n_01       0     
#>  N          40    
#> 
#> Confidence level: 95%
ci_proportion_paired(n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, N = 40, method = "wald")
#>  term       value
#>  ci_lower   0.000
#>  difference 0.000
#>  ci_upper   0.000
#>  n_10       0    
#>  n_01       0    
#>  N          40   
#> 
#> Confidence level: 95%
